name: Gangotri Dham–Lakhnadon Highway
aka: Formed mainly from stretches of the former NH 108, NH 94, NH 58, NH 119, NH 91 and NH 86

timeline.event: Char Dham road project launched, widening the Rishikesh–Gangotri stretch of the highway

history: NH 34 starts high in the Himalayas at Gangotri Dham, one of the four Char Dham pilgrimage shrines, and follows the Bhagirathi (Ganga) valley down to Rishikesh and Haridwar. It then crosses the plains of western Uttar Pradesh through Meerut, Aligarh and Kanpur, and climbs into the Bundelkhand hills and central Madhya Pradesh. The route was pieced together in the 2010s renumbering by joining several older highways, and it ends at Lakhnadon, where it meets NH 44.
facts: At about 1,426 km, it links a Himalayan shrine with the centre of India.
Its mountain stretch from Rishikesh up to Gangotri is part of the Char Dham pilgrimage road network.
Haridwar, one of the holiest cities on the Ganga, sits on its route.
It ends at Lakhnadon on NH 44, India's longest national highway.
Most of the highway is a two-lane road.

sources.title: NHAI — National Highways Authority of India
